# Testament of Issachar — 5
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Cantabrigiensis) | **Section:** Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs

---

**1** The record of the words of Issachar. For he called his sons and said unto them: **2** Hearken, my children, to Issachar your father; give heed to the words of him who is beloved of the Lord. **3** I was born the fifth son to Jacob as a reward for the mandrakes. **4** For Reuben my brother brought mandrakes from the field, and Rachel met him and took them. **5** And Reuben wept, and at his voice Leah my mother came forth. **6** Now these mandrakes were sweet-smelling apples which were produced in the land of Haran below a ravine of water. **7** And Rachel said: I will not give them to thee, but they shall be to me instead of children. For the Lord had made Rachel barren. **8** And Leah said: Let Jacob be thine this night for thy son's mandrakes. **9** And Rachel said to her: Let him be thine this night for thy son's mandrakes. **10** And Jacob knew Leah that night, and she conceived and bore me, and on account of the reward she called my name Issachar.

**2** Then came an angel of the Lord to Leah, and said: Two children more shalt thou bear, since thou hast given to thy sister the mandrakes because of thy modesty. **2** And she who had been made barren shall also bear four children; for the Lord hath heard her prayer. **3** And it was so; for when Rachel had the mandrakes, she gave Jacob to Leah for a night, and he lay with her. **4** And God hearkened to Rachel also, for she desired the fruit of the womb and not pleasure, and she bare Joseph and Benjamin.

**3** And my father loved me because I was born in simplicity; and I was not crafty in mine actions, but upright. **2** I tilled the ground; I brought to my father the fruits of the field in their season. **3** And my father blessed me, for he saw that I walked in rectitude before him. **4** And I was not a busybody in my doings, nor envious of my neighbour, nor did I slander any man; **5** I walked not in haughtiness of heart; but I was a lover of God and of men, and in compassion I gave of the fruit of the earth to every poor man and to every one in distress.

**4** Hear me therefore, my children, and walk in simplicity of heart, performing righteousness before God and man; love ye one another, and whatsoever things ye do, do them in truth before God. **2** For in these things will the Lord bless you with good things for ever. **3** For the Lord honoureth a simple man who giveth not heed to an evil thought against his neighbour; he hath no desire in his mind to defraud another man, nor to overreach or oppress any one; but he walketh in singleness of life, looking only to what is good even for the brute creation. **4** Guard therefore, my children, all the law of the Lord, and seek simplicity, and walk in guilelessness, not playing the busybody with the business of your neighbour. **5** But love the Lord and your neighbour, have compassion on the poor and weak.

**5** Bow down your back to farming, and toil in labours in all manner of husbandry, offering gifts in thankfulness to the Lord. **2** For with the first-fruits of the earth will the Lord bless you, even as He blessed all the saints from Abel even until now. **3** For no portion was given to you save of the fatness of the earth, whose fruits are raised by toil. **4** For our father Jacob blessed me with blessings of the earth and of firstfruits.

**6** And Levi and Judah were glorified by the Lord even in the midst of their brethren; and the Lord chose them. **2** And flee, therefore, my children, all jealousy and envy, and walk in simplicity of soul and without dissimulation, keeping yourselves from all sins of the spirit of Beliar. **3** For I myself have done these things before the Lord, and have rejoiced; and neither have I been led astray by the devices of men, nor do I know that I have sinned grievously.

**7** All my days I kept truth, for I loved the Lord with all my strength; likewise also I loved every man as I love my own children. **2** Do ye also these things, my children, and every spirit of Beliar shall flee from you, and no deed of wicked men shall have dominion over you; and every wild beast shall ye subdue, since ye have with you the God of heaven and earth and walk with men in singleness of heart. **3** And when he had said these things, he commanded his sons that they should carry him up to Hebron and bury him there with his fathers. And he stretched out his feet and fell asleep in peace.

---
*End of Testament of Issachar*
